title: RHOMBIS: A Real Angled Bridge
items: New: Multi-Cell's two real cells each get a third real alternate fill option -- a diagonal octahedron, a real bipyramid through that cell's own center, built along the exact real neighbor axis the two cells share (facePieces(), the same real primitive verified earlier the same day for the Disphenoid crossover's own interlocking tabs). Genuinely different from Stage 2's own plain Octahedron (built along a cube-face axis, dead straight relative to the RD's own faces) -- this one runs along a real 12-neighbor diagonal instead, so it reads as visibly tilted/angled. Direct instruction: "multi cell could benefit from a variety of pieces within it", generalized immediately after into a real standing idea worth reusing elsewhere: "the bridging point of any adjacent shapes in a structure is a potential opportunity for a big odd connection."

New: a fourth alternate fill, a flat star -- a real, much SHORTER pyramid off the exact same real shared face, reaching only halfway toward each cell's own center rather than all the way to it. This cell's own star and its real neighbor's own star (built the same way, off the same real face) meet exactly there and together read as one flat, wide, 4-pointed star/diamond rather than a tall gem -- direct instruction: "a nice flat square star shape that spans halfway into two joined cells".

title: RHOMBIS: Multi-Cell Was Out of Place
items: Fixed: Multi-Cell -- 26 real pieces to place, the single highest piece count of any stage in the entire game (every other stage tops out at 17) -- sat right after Conjoined Pieces, out of order with the rest of its own small tier (One Piece, Octahedron, Cube, Conjoined Pieces, Rhombic Dodecahedron: the same real loose-pyramid/fused-whole-cell choice at 1 or 2 real lattice cells). Caught directly: "stage 22 is more complex than several of the puzzles following it by amount of pieces to place."

Corrected in two passes, not one: piece count alone isn't the whole story -- comparing it against genuinely different mechanisms (key/decoy/crossover tiers) elsewhere in the game was the wrong axis ("it should have still been in same group as before, as its only a repeated procedure and similar piece it doesnt deserve represrenting highest difficulty"). Piece count only means something WITHIN a shared mechanism family -- exactly why Salt/Calcite were ordered ahead of the larger Alloy stages earlier the same day. Multi-Cell now sits last in its own real family instead, by real piece count (1, 2, 6, 7, 12, 26), with Conjoined Pieces and Rhombic Dodecahedron also swapped into correct ascending order along the way.

title: RHOMBIS: Real Flat Contact, Not Points
items: Fixed: a real geometry bug in the Big Hull + Disphenoid crossover puzzles' brand new interlocking tabs (shipped earlier the same day) -- they were built from the wrong 6-direction frame (the same one disphenoids themselves use, which is real, but for a DIFFERENT real relationship: the octahedral/BCC-interstitial directions, not the FCC lattice's own 12 real nearest-neighbor directions). Two chunks built that way could only ever touch at a single point, never a real flat face -- caught directly: "connecting disphenoids / flat octahedra by points doesnt translate as valid... only ever connect by flats".

Fixed properly, not patched: a real new shared primitive (facePieces(), core/lattice.js) decomposes a cell into its own actual 12 rhombic faces -- the exact faces two real adjacent cells share -- verified numerically (each face a genuine planar rhombus, facing its own real neighbor direction, and the 12 of them together reconstructing the exact same cell volume the existing 6-pyramid decomposition already does) rather than trusted by eye. The interlocking tabs now come from a cell's own real shared face with its real neighbor, guaranteed flat contact by construction -- confirmed end-to-end: a cell's face slice and its neighbor's own matching slice share the exact same 4 real-world points.

title: RHOMBIS: A Real Difficulty Curve
items: Fixed: stage order is a whole-game difficulty curve now, not a per-tier one -- BCC's own 1- and 2-piece introduction had ended up stranded as the SECOND-TO-LAST and LAST stages in the entire game, right after two 22/23-piece crossover puzzles, so a player sampling "the hard end" could land on a 1-piece stage and reasonably conclude the whole game was trivial. Moved beside the equivalent FCC introduction near the very start instead.

Fixed: the same real problem, smaller scale -- the Alloy tier's own Salt and Calcite puzzles (8 real pieces each) sat AFTER the larger 14-17 piece metal alloys purely because of which real-world family got scoped first, not because they were harder. Reordered the whole tier to genuinely ascend by real piece count.

Fixed: Crystal: Copper (a real recolored Big Hull: Cuboctahedron, no key, identical mechanism) was stranded at the very end alongside the hardest crossover puzzles despite matching its own un-recolored twin's difficulty exactly -- moved to sit right beside it.

Redesigned: the Big Hull + Disphenoid crossover puzzles. The previous version decomposed a whole cell into 18-24 separate small disphenoid pieces, which read as a second, unrelated mini-jigsaw bolted onto one lucky cell rather than a real interlocking key. Chunks now interlock directly at real crossing points instead: a genuine boundary cell between two chunks (found via the same real lattice adjacency the chunk partition itself grows through) splits along its own 3 real axis-pairs, and each slice is folded straight into whichever neighboring chunk actually borders it there -- a real "half a cell missing, supplied by its neighbor" seam, with zero new pieces added.

Fixed: two real instances of the same underlying mistake -- a piece bound to one arbitrary matching location when an identical piece should be able to fill ANY identical open location (Multi-Cell's two identical fused whole-cell pieces, and would-be duplicate disphenoid pieces in the redesign above) -- found and corrected across the file, not just where first reported.

title: Naming a Real Honeycomb
items: Documentation only, no behavior change: Cuboctahedron Build growing face-to-face plus its own Octahedron gap-fill piece (shipped 2026-08-31, "Cuboctahedra, Face to Face") has a real, established name in solid geometry we'd never actually stated -- a rectified cubic honeycomb, the vertex-truncated form of the plain cubic honeycomb, built here as a real, numerically zero-gap tiling rather than an approximation.

Worth being explicit about since it's genuinely easy to miss otherwise: the plain (un-rectified) cubic honeycomb underneath it is itself real and already reachable in this same World, no separate system needed -- Lattice Quick-View's own Cube mode already renders the exact inscribed cube each lattice point needs; placed at both of the parities Cuboctahedron/Octahedron already use, those cubes tile with zero gap on their own.

The same real structure shows up a second time, independently: Rhombis's new Salt puzzle is built on rock-salt-lattice.js, which proves sodium chloride's own two ion sublattices are, combined, this identical simple-cubic lattice -- verified numerically there too, not assumed.

title: RHOMBIS: Real Alloys and Salt
items: New: a real Alloy tier -- 3 ordered intermetallics (nickel aluminide, iron aluminide, beta brass), 2 dilute alloy steels (chromium, molybdenum -- which cells are the alloying metal is drawn fresh at random every playthrough), a real interstitial Carbon Steel (the actual octahedral gap carbon occupies in iron, a genuinely different piece of geometry, not a recolored cell), and 4 real gold/copper alloys (electrum, white gold, rose gold, bronze) -- every composition a real, verified ratio, not an invented one.

New: Salt -- a real sodium chloride puzzle, 1 ion and its 6 real neighbors in a genuine octahedral cross. Built on a brand new shared math module proving something real, not assumed: table salt's own crystal structure is the same FCC lattice already used everywhere else in this game, just with its own internal gaps filled by a second ion -- so every ion's own natural shape turns out to be a plain cube, nothing new to build.
New: the previous 17 near-identical single-metal stages merged down to 2, each one now honestly naming every other real metal it also represents instead of shipping a separate stage per element.

New: an easier Color Match tier duplicating the very first shapes with real colored pieces instead of shape-matching alone, positioned right before the harder originals rather than after everything else.

Fixed: two real color bugs caught by actually playing -- a colored piece's own background region wasn't tinted to match it (reading as visually clashing, especially on darker metals), and the colored-match tier's own palette was getting overridden by the game's ordinary right/wrong flash the moment you picked up a piece, which also secretly gave the answer away.

title: RHOMBIS: A Second Real Lattice
items: New: BCC -- a genuinely different real crystal lattice alongside FCC, with its own real space-filling shape (a truncated octahedron, not a rhombic dodecahedron) and its own real 8+6 neighbor geometry, not a reskin of the existing content.

New: Crystal tier -- real FCC and BCC coordination geometry, each colored with a real crystallizing metal's own characteristic color (later merged into 2 stages carrying the other real metals as attributions, and followed by a dedicated Alloy tier -- see the next update).

New: 4 crossover tiers combining mechanics that never met before -- a Burr Puzzle key layered onto a Molecule Split, a Mirrored Molecule, and a Branching Molecule composite, plus a Big Hull variant where the key can hide among either a plain chunk or genuine fine-grained disphenoid detail, drawn fresh at random every time you play.
New: any stage built by combining earlier ones now shows real lineage in the stage picker -- which tier(s) it draws from, by name and number.

Fixed: a Burr-key stage caught giving away which piece was blocked just from its own shape, before any placement was even tried -- the key is now drawn from every real piece in the stage, not always the same category of piece.
Fixed: two stage names that spelled out exactly which piece held the hidden key, defeating the whole point of a Burr puzzle.
Fixed: a redundant crossover variant, found to be a strict subset of a stronger one already shipped -- removed rather than kept as weaker filler.

title: RHOMBIS: Eighty-Five Puzzles Deep
items: New: RHOMBIS grew from 16 stages to 85 in one sitting, real-time play-tested the whole way through. Difficulty now genuinely ramps with stage number -- simple whole-shape arrangement first, real orientation-matching next, and increasingly large/irregular composite puzzles at the top.

New: Molecules -- two real shapes joined into one bigger piece, solved by placing exactly the two pieces that make it, against decoys drawn from the same shape family. Every possible pairing from the game's own shape catalog is a real, distinct stage.

New: Mirrored Molecule -- a molecule whose two halves are genuine mirror images of each other, not just a rotated copy. Only a handful of this lattice's real shapes are actually chiral (can't be rotated onto their own reflection); each one gets a real stage here.

New: Hulls and Big Hulls -- a single shape broken into 2-4 real sub-pieces instead of a shape being joined to another, up through a real 13-cell Cuboctahedron and a 20-cell tetrahedral stack, the biggest targets in the game.
New: Branching Molecules -- three shapes joined at a shared hub instead of two in a line, a genuine Y-shaped composite.
New: a whole rhombic dodecahedron decomposed into 24 real tetragonal disphenoids instead of the usual 12 pyramids -- a completely different way to build the same familiar shape.

New: Burr Puzzles -- the first stages where placement ORDER matters. A "key" piece genuinely won't seat until the others around it are in place, with a real explanation on screen if you try it out of turn, not just a silent rejection.

Fixed: several real bugs caught mid-session by actually playing the new stages, not just building them -- pieces silently missing their own tray tap target when their visual center didn't match their logical one, a tray that stacked every piece in one long column regardless of how many there were, and an orientation scheme on two stages that quietly had duplicate entries pointing at the same real pose.

title: RHOMBIS: A New Way In
items: New: RHOMBIS, a short geometric-packing puzzle that introduces the game's core pyramid-to-cube-to-rhombic-dodecahedron relationships -- rotate a target shape, tap pieces into place, and watch it build from a single pyramid up through an octahedron and a cube. Wrong orientations are flagged red, valid ones green, right on the shape itself. Linked from the welcome screen; built mobile/touch-first from the start.
Fixed: completing a cube's very last missing pyramid could occasionally spawn an unrelated stray piece elsewhere instead of finishing the block you were actually working on.
Fixed: a leftover "no pyramid there" message could linger on screen well after it stopped being true, making a successful placement look like it hadn't worked.

title: See It Through, Any Shape
items: Spherical Toggle and World View now work together properly: switch to Skeleton while Spherical is on and every ghosted shape shows as a real wireframe sphere, not the original angular piece -- flip Spherical on or off while Skeleton is already showing and it updates immediately.

Fixed: Translucent mode had no visible effect at all -- materials were changing correctly under the hood but the render never picked it up. Now genuinely see-through, with real colors showing through overlapping pieces (not just a generic fade).
Fixed: picking Cuboctahedron from the Piece wheel opened its color picker behind the wheel itself, making it impossible to click. The wheel now closes first, same as every other Piece pick.
Auto-assign material by piece type now defaults on, with all 8 per-piece colors adjustable in Settings -- manual picking is still one click away.

title: A Fuller Palette
items: Four new materials: Amethyst, Rose Quartz, Citrine, and Turquoise -- same real-mineral naming as Garnet, Emerald, and Gold, now 14 colors deep.

New Auto-assign option next to the material picker: turn it on and every piece type (RD, Cube, Pyramid, Truncated Octahedron, Flattened Octahedron, Disphenoid, Octahedron, Cuboctahedron) places with its own fixed default material, no manual picking needed.

New World View toggle -- the three-rings symbol on the corner HUD wheel -- switches your whole build between Color (normal), Translucent (every material, Glassite included, actually see-through for the first time), and Skeleton (ghost fill plus a real edge outline, matching the Rhombic Wheel's own look).

title: New Faces on the Wheel
items: Settings is now a real gear -- bold, centered, and easy to spot at a glance instead of a small faint glyph.
Cyborg has a proper symbol: a Metropolis-inspired robot head, stepped headphone-style ears and all.
Smooth is now a hexagon touching its own circle from the inside, one clean blended line -- not the barely-there rounded hexagon it used to be.
Blueprint's icon is a pair of dividing compasses now, not an unclear tick-marked line.
Dropped the faint circle that used to sit behind every hexagon icon on the wheel -- just the hexagon now, noticeably sharper.
Boosted contrast on several corner-HUD symbols (Spherical, X-Ray, Reload, BCC Lattice) that were hard to make out against the medallion.

title: A Simpler Wheel
items: Two departments retired: Construct (a pure hop with no content of its own) and Rhombisis (three of its four faces just duplicated tools already on Build, Blueprint, and Cultivate). Build and Alter now sit directly on Home; BCC Build moved there too.
Every wheel shows real content the moment you land on it now, not a blank face mixed in with the first ones you see.
"Rhombitect" and "Rhombivate" are now Blueprint and Cultivate -- plain English, matching the rest of the wheel. "Lab / Settings" is just Settings everywhere.

The welcome screen's ENTER is a large, always-clickable label now, fixed at the center of the rotating logo -- no more waiting for a swinging face to catch it, and the old pulsing glow faces are gone.

title: Never Wonder Where the Wheel Went
items: Generating a body right where you're standing can still fill your whole view -- a toast now confirms it happened and reminds you Tab or Menu still opens the wheel from there.

title: See It Round: Spherical Toggle
items: New view toggle on the corner HUD wheel: render your whole build in a simplified, near-spherical form -- every real piece (RD, Cube, Octahedron, Cuboctahedron, Truncated Octahedron, Disphenoid, and every Pyramid combination in between) shown as a sphere, sized by its own real volume. Most pieces are also capped at the exact distance to their nearest same-type neighbor, so they never overlap no matter how densely you've built -- Disphenoid is the one exception, always shown at full size. A client-side view only -- your actual cells are completely untouched, flip it off any time.

A lone Pyramid or a cube with only some of its 6 pyramids on gets sized the same principled way -- 6 pyramids with no cube lands at exactly Cube's own size (they're the same real volume), and the full 12-pyramid build lands at exactly RD's.
Every Disphenoid (including all 4 in a Flattened Octahedron) renders at its own full, real-volume size -- no holding back for nearby neighbors.

title: Pyramid: A Firm Foundation
items: The Pyramid piece is Rhombiverse's real foundational cell: one stands alone, two bond together (flat-to-flat into a free octahedron, or point-to-point to keep chaining outward), six form a cube, and twelve build up into a full Rhombic Dodecahedron -- the same single piece scales into every core shape here, Cuboctahedra included.

Fixed: bonding a second pyramid onto an existing lone one now correctly builds outward -- flat-to-flat and point-to-point placement both work as intended, instead of misplacing the new pyramid back on the same cell.

title: Cuboctahedra, Face to Face
items: Cuboctahedron Build can now grow face to face with its neighbors, not just corner to corner -- click closer to a flat face on an existing one instead of a point to grow that way, filling in the space between them.

New Piece: Octahedron -- fills the gap that opens up between cuboctahedra face to face. Select it and click near a Cuboctahedron's own corner. A real, exact fit, not a rough approximation -- and separate from the existing Flattened Octahedron (renamed from Octahedron Site, to be less easily confused with the new one), which still builds the same BCC-interstitial bundle it always has.

The Piece wheel's own Material face is gone -- picking any Piece now opens the color swatch right after, so shape and material stay a single step apart. Material's still one tap away from the bottom-left color icon too.

title: Grow It Your Way
items: New Cultivate sliders: Growth limit, Growth rate, and Bias, alongside the existing Direction and Packing density -- shape how far, how fast, and which way a manually-planted seed grows, no genome required.
New hint in the Lab panel's Piece picker: try placing 6 pyramids on a cube, then 12, then remove the outer 6 -- a small nudge toward one of this tool's favorite tricks.

title: Just the Shape, No Strings Attached
items: New: Export Model (.rhomb) in the Lab panel -- a pure-geometry export of your cells and any grown seeds, with none of your claims, inventory, trades, or organism data along for the ride. Export World is unchanged, still there for the full picture.

title: Cuboctahedron on the Piece Wheel
items: Cuboctahedron Build now has its own real seat on the Piece picker wheel -- click a face of your normal World to place one, or near a point of an existing one to grow toward that neighbor.
Made room by retiring "Lenses" from the shared universal ring across every wheel -- X-Ray is still one tap away via the corner HUD wheel and the Lab panel.

title: A Second Lattice, Point to Point
items: New: Cuboctahedron Build (Rhombeometry mode) -- a real, persistent world of vertex-pointed cuboctahedra sitting alongside your normal Rhombic Dodecahedron World, the RD lattice's own dual shape.
Cuboctahedron also joins Lattice View's set of preview lenses, and the corner HUD wheel's Lattice View face now reflects whichever mode is currently active.

title: Smoother, Steadier Rendering
items: Fixed: overlapping translucent surfaces in Lattice View and Dualize Preview could flicker/shimmer against your real World and against each other, most visible together with X-Ray. A real rendering issue, now resolved.

title: X-Ray, All the Way Through
items: Fixed: X-Ray's cross-section used to skip BCC, Octahedron Site, Disphenoid, and Pyramid pieces entirely -- added after X-Ray itself, they never respected the cutaway plane. X-Ray now cuts cleanly through everything you've built.

title: One Lens for Every Shape
items: New Lattice View: a third icon next to Menu, bottom-left, cycling through a real preview lens for every Piece type -- RD, Cube, and Pyramid shown on your own built World, then BCC/TO, Octahedron Site, and Disphenoid, then Off.
Replaces the old BCC-only lens and the standalone Interpenetrating Lattice Preview, both retired -- this one covers everything they did and more, across your whole structure rather than just nearby.

title: A Cleaner HUD
items: Removed the top-right "Mode · Material" text -- redundant now that the bottom-left quick-select icons already show your current Piece/Material at a glance.
The Lab panel now has its own close (✕) button, matching every other panel.

title: New Colors to Build With
items: Two new buildable materials: Emerald and Gold, right alongside Base Rhomb and the rest in the Material picker.

title: Know What You're Holding
items: Fixed: Home and Piece > RD used the same plain hexagon icon on the wheel, easy to mix up at a glance. Home is now a clear "H" in its own hexagon.
Fixed: Material's own wheel icon (three same-color wedges) was hard to identify or remember. It's now three real material-colored swatches instead.
Material is now also a choice right on the Piece wheel, not just over on Build -- pick your shape and color in the same place.
Picking a shape no longer closes the wheel straight away, so you can pick a Material right after without reopening anything.
New: two small icons next to Menu always show your current Piece and Material. Tap either to jump straight back to that picker.

title: Steady as You Rotate
items: Fixed: on iPad/iPhone, dragging to rotate the corner HUD wheel could also spin your whole World's camera along with it. Rotating the HUD wheel now only moves the HUD wheel.

title: Straight to the Point
items: Fixed: opening a department on the Rhombic Wheel (Build > Piece, or any other) used to leave the wheel exactly as rotated as it was when you clicked -- often an edge-on view where nothing in the new department was actually visible yet, needing an extra drag just to see what you'd chosen. Every department now opens facing you clearly, the same clean view the wheel itself opens with.

title: Never Truly Empty
items: Fixed: removing your very last cell used to leave your World with nothing left to click -- Add had no face to place against, a genuine dead end. Your World now always keeps at least one real cell, restored automatically the instant it would otherwise hit zero, so there's always something to build forward from.
Same fix for BCC Build and the interstitial lattice (Octahedron Site / Disphenoid) -- whichever one you're working in always keeps at least one real piece to build forward from too.

Fixed: Clear World left that one real cell exactly where it always is, but never brought your camera/view back to it -- if you'd wandered off elsewhere first, the cell existed but sat off-screen, unreachable, indistinguishable from actually being stuck. Clear World now resets your view (and exits Walk mode if it was on) to look straight at it every time.

title: Real Cells, Not Just a Preview
items: Two new real, placeable pieces (Piece picker, Rhombeometry): Disphenoid and Octahedron Site -- the genuine BCC interstitial-site tessellation (the same octahedral/tetrahedral geometry carbon actually sits in inside iron), not a view-only overlay.
Disphenoid places one at a time; Octahedron Site places the 4-disphenoid bundle they combine into in one click. Both grow by clicking an existing one's own face, same as every other piece type.
Builds freely on top of your FCC and BCC worlds -- overlap between all three lattices is expected, not prevented.

Piece is a real destination on the main Rhombic Wheel now, not a separate popup -- open it the same way as any other department (Build > Piece) to reach all 6 pieces (RD, Cube, Pyramid, Truncated Octahedron, Octahedron Site, Disphenoid) by rotating the one real wheel, same as everywhere else in the app.

title: Where the Two Lattices Meet
items: New Interpenetrating Lattice preview (Rhombeometry, Lab panel): shows real BCC/truncated-octahedron cells nested exactly inside your own build, wherever a cell sits at a coordinate that can host one -- each RD's 6 sharp vertices meet a TO's 6 square-face centers exactly.
View-only -- nothing is written to your World.

title: Dualize Works Both Ways Now
items: Dualize Preview now reacts to whichever lattice you actually click -- click an FCC structure to preview it as BCC/TO, or click a real placed BCC/TO cell (from BCC Build) to preview it back as FCC.
Still view-only both ways -- nothing is written to your World either direction.

title: Small Fixes, Real Polish
items: Fixed: switching the dual-lattice view mode quickly could leave a stale preview on screen even after choosing FCC only.
Fixed: the corner HUD wheel's own background could mismatch the World behind it -- it now always matches exactly.
Fixed: the corner HUD wheel looked flat when still -- it now reads as a real 3D shape at rest, not just while spinning.
Fixed: touching the screen on iPhone/iPad could bring up text-selection/Copy -- disabled everywhere except real text fields (like your own AI key).

title: Every Piece, Visible
items: Fixed: the Piece picker (Build -> Piece) was showing its wireframe diamond net with no icons at all -- RD, Cube, Pyramid, and Truncated Octahedron now all show their real shape icon in their own diamond, as intended.
Fixed: RD's own icon blended into its frame and read as blank -- it's a clear solid shape now.
Fixed: all 4 icons sat slightly above center in their diamond -- they're precisely centered now.

title: Steady Under Load
items: New optional FPS meter in the Lab panel (off by default) shows your real frame rate.
Graphics quality now steps itself down automatically if your frame rate stays low for a few seconds -- and you can always turn it back up yourself in Settings.
Importing or loading a very large World now warns you first, since it may run slowly on lower-power devices.

title: A Truly Blank Canvas
items: First-time Rhombeometry visitors now land on a single cell in empty space, not the pre-built Showcase World and its guided tour -- geometry really does come first now.
Full World's first visit is unchanged.

title: Dualize: See Your Build the Other Way
items: New Dualize Preview (Rhombeometry, Lab panel): click any structure you've built to preview it reinterpreted through the dual body-centered-cubic lattice -- your own build, seen through the other order.
View-only for now -- nothing is written to your World, just a real overlay you can look at and clear.

title: A Still Place to Build
items: New Model workspace setting (Lab panel): freezes growth, ecosystem catch-up, asteroid regrowth, and inventory decay so nothing moves on its own while you work -- geometry and material tools stay fully available.
The Rhombic Wheel reacts live: Model workspace quiets Rhombivate, Trade, Explore, Plant a Seed, and BCC Build, leaving Construct, Rhombitect, and the rest of Rhombisis front and center.
Switch back to World workspace anytime -- nothing is lost, everything just picks back up.

title: Five Lenses on Your Lattice
items: The BCC Lattice toggle now cycles through five real views instead of one: FCC only, the dual lattice only, both together in distinct colors, or either one ghosted behind the other.
Seeing both lattices together now uses a real color-and-outline pairing, not color alone.

title: Every Piece, One Set of Buttons
items: New Pyramid piece: shave individual pyramids off a placed block, or add them back one at a time -- real texture and detail no whole-block tool could reach before.
New Cube piece: place a bare block with no pyramids at all, a lighter starting shape to build up from scratch with the Pyramid piece above.

Add and Remove are universal now -- one pair of buttons for RD, Cube, Pyramid, and the BCC Truncated Octahedron, switched with a single Piece picker instead of six separate buttons that did overlapping jobs under different names.
Touch: tap to Add, hold to Remove -- works the same way across every piece type now.
Wheel symbols sit exactly centered on their own face at any angle, and their labels no longer hide under your touching hand.

title: True to Form
items: BCC Build (Rhombeometry, Lab panel): place real, saved cells on the dual body-centered-cubic lattice alongside your normal World -- click a face to extend it, or a face of your own build to start one nearby. The two lattices are free to overlap where they meet, on purpose, so they read as one joined structure.
The welcome screen is a large rotating wireframe rhombic dodecahedron now, with ENTER living right on the shape itself -- two of its own faces light up as they turn to face you.
Your view now picks up exactly where you left it on your next visit, instead of resetting to the same default spot every time.

title: One wheel, everywhere
items: The old flat menu is gone -- the Rhombic Wheel in 3D is now the only way to navigate, covering every department, tool, and picker the old one did.
A new Rhombisis department gathers Sculpt, Generate a Body, and Plant a Seed in one place -- the three ways to bring something new into being.

A small gold Rhombic Wheel now sits permanently in the corner, replacing the old row of separate buttons -- rotate it by hand to reach Lab, X-Ray, Cyborg, Sculpture Mode, Duality, BCC, Clear World, and Reload.
Every open face on both wheels now shows something -- a temporary shortcut to a real function elsewhere -- instead of sitting blank.

title: The wheel becomes the shape
items: A new toggle in the top-right opens the Rhombic Wheel in 3D -- navigate Build, Alter, Rhombitect, Cultivate, and Trade on the real rhombic-dodecahedron shape itself, not a flat menu.
Every department does real things -- pick a material, generate a celestial body, choose a species to plant, dig, smooth, fill, sculpt -- right alongside the existing wheel, not replacing it yet.
Lenses, Cyborg, Lab Settings, and the Almanac are reachable from every wheel, in the exact same spot every time.

title: A second lattice, and an easy reset
items: New BCC Lattice toggle (Rhombeometry mode) shows a real, connected finer lattice running through your build -- a client-side view only, your World stays untouched.
Clear World and Reload are now always-visible HUD buttons, instead of buried in Lab Settings.

title: Rhombeometry, right from the start
items: A real Mode choice now exists: Rhombeometry (geometry only) or Full World (mining, trade, hazards) -- pick it on the welcome screen or flip it anytime from Lab Settings.
New visitors land in Rhombeometry by default, since the geometry comes first.
Switching modes never wipes anything -- your World's own cells, claims, and belts just sit inert while their systems are off, the same clean hide every individual system already got.

title: Sculpture Mode, truly its own space
items: Sculpture Mode no longer shows the real World's presets or asteroid-belt hints -- it's a genuinely isolated scratch space now, not just in spirit.

Cyborg Mode's AI assistance (Semi- and Full-Cyborg) is now dual-aware -- build outward along a cube or octahedron vertex and it can suggest completing that whole inscribed solid, not just a mirror-plane edge.
Claims and Load-World presets now hide cleanly when their systems are off, instead of leaving a broken button behind.

title: The geometry comes first
items: Rhombiverse is now explicit about what it is: an instrument for exploring and sculpting rhombic-dodecahedron space -- the FCC lattice geometry is the core, not the mining/trade/hazard systems built on top of it.
A features.js flag registry lets some of those systems (Achievements, Animals, Hydrosphere, Trade decay) load only when needed, instead of always-on.

New in Sculpture Mode: the cube and octahedron inscribed in every block, made visible and sculptable -- a Show Dual overlay, Snap to Dual, a Dual Shell brush, Cube/Octa symmetry presets, and Full symmetry (48).

title: Walk anywhere, mine anywhere
items: Walk Mode now works on touch -- a virtual joystick and jump button, not just keyboard and mouse.
Fixed mining while walking, and asteroid belts disappearing after Load/New World or a Shared World switch.

title: The Rhombic Wheel, and everything behind it
items: One control surface for everything: the Rhombic Wheel (Tab / Space, or tap Menu) replaces the old always-visible sidebar.
Sculpt: a real symmetry/mirror tool with Model and Chisel modes, plus a standalone Sculpture Mode scratch workspace.
Grow: Cultivate real aperiodic growth, and see the tiling a structure casts with Duality Mode.
Cyborg Mode: an optional guided walkthrough, plus real AI assistance for Sculpt/Cultivate -- bring your own API key or use the shared one, never required to use.
Achievements, World sharing via a link, a public Gallery of shared Worlds, and a sequenced first-visit tour instead of a tutorial modal.
Walk up to another person and Interact to trade -- named avatars, a lightweight pseudonymous display name, no accounts.
A pass of real mobile/touch fixes: tap-to-open the wheel, bottom-sheet tool panels, first-use hints on the icon toggles.

title: Growth, evolution, and a home to explore
items: Real aperiodic (Penrose/Ammann-rhombohedra) growth -- plant a seed and watch it unfold into a tree, shell, or crystal cluster over time.
A genome/phenotype evolution system: planted organisms reproduce, mutate, and speciate on their own.
Animals: habitats, mobility, and real herbivore/carnivore relationships.
A Showcase World -- a real continental planetoid with growth, evolved organisms, and animals already in it.

title: Whole planets, gravity, and the extremes of physics
items: Planetoid building with real radial gravity bending toward the core.
Water and ice, black holes, star systems, and supernovae -- each grounded in real physics (Schwarzschild behavior, Chandrasekhar-limit detonation, icy-moon subsurface oceans).
Shared World: opt-in realtime multiplayer, ownership claims, mining, and barter trade.
Public deploy, with the legal/safety basics (Terms, Privacy, Security) in place.

title: Rhombiverse begins
items: The first block: a rhombic dodecahedron lattice you can build outward from, face by face.
Local save/load, export/import as plain JSON.
